summary: Genuine counter-evidence search attempted for all six target claims from counter-evidence-plan.md, split into 7 scored counter-claim records (target claim C was split into its two distinct sub-assertions: the FPS figure and the bento-grid-density question). Findings: (A) chart-type superiority -- a 2025 peer-reviewed SAGE study (Hill) plus classic Simkin & Hastie and Kosara/Skau research found pie charts about as accurate as bar charts for proportion estimation and found angle (the usual justification for anti-pie-chart guidance) is the least reliable pie-chart cue -- genuine, fairly strong complicating evidence (0.7). (B) dark-mode contrast ceiling -- accessibility specialists (Stephanie Walter and others) document a halation effect for users with astigmatism and argue against forcing maximum contrast, a real but moderate complicating factor rather than a flat contradiction of Material Design's number (0.55). (C1) Studio Meyer's specific 15-30% FPS figure -- no independent, authoritative source (web.dev, MDN) gives any quantitative figure at all; other sources citing similar numbers are low-tier and uncited, so the figure remains genuinely unverified either way, confirming the brief's own flagged risk rather than resolving it (0.25). (C2) bento-grid density at high information density -- no credible source was found either way; the one relevant claim traces to a low-reliability, uncited design-agency blog, so this open question from the brief remains open (0.15) -- both C sub-findings are reportable as 'no credible verification found' rather than failures. (D) skeleton vs. spinner preference -- a direct controlled study (Viget, n=136) found skeleton screens underperformed spinners and blank screens on every metric, real empirical counter-evidence though the authors call it preliminary (0.6). (E) content-form-fit distinctiveness -- NN/g's own 'Fresh vs. Familiar' research argues familiarity should dominate for high-frequency-use interfaces, a same-tier, on-point complicating source, though it addresses redesign/change generally rather than dashboard genericness specifically (0.5). (F) non-zero Y-axis anti-pattern -- recognized data-viz authorities (Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic citing Stephen Few, and Alberto Cairo) explicitly permit non-zero baselines for line charts/trend widgets under specific conditions while keeping the zero-baseline rule strict for bar charts, narrowing the brief's unqualified framing (0.65). No claim was found to be flatly wrong; all seven records land in the 'true but overstated / context-dependent' or 'genuinely unverified either way' categories consistent with the plan's stated expectations, and no false balance was manufactured -- weak or absent findings (C1, C2) were reported as such rather than stretched.
